meta.name: Strategy IQ
meta.disclaimer: This diagnostic provides strategic advisory guidance to support enterprise IT strategy, Target Operating Model (TOM), application rationalization, tech debt sizing, and board-level investment governance. It does not constitute a formal legal or financial audit.

sections.title: Business-IT Alignment & Co-Design
sections.desc: Coupling between technology investments and enterprise P&L growth strategies.

sections.desc: Product-led squad structures, platform-as-a-product, and decision autonomy.

questions.q: How intentionally is IT strategy coupled with enterprise business strategy?
questions.hint: Evaluates whether technology is treated as a back-office cost center or a co-author of market differentiation.

opts.text: Level 1 · Nascent: Isolated IT roadmap with zero reference to business P&L outcomes
Level 2 · Emerging: Periodic presentation of IT plans with loose references to corporate goals
Level 3 · Established: Documented alignment matrices mapping projects to strategic priorities
Level 4 · Advanced: Shared OKRs and joint accountability between IT and business executives
Level 5 · Leading: Continuous co-design where technology directly originates new revenue models

questions.q: What is the strategic review cadence for technology roadmaps?
questions.hint: Frequency of recalibration against market shifts, competitor moves, and macro dynamics.

descs: Level 1 · Nascent: Multi-year static plan rarely revisited until crises occur
Level 2 · Emerging: Annual defensive review aligned strictly to budget calendar
Level 3 · Established: Twice-yearly structured executive architectural health reviews
Level 4 · Advanced: Quarterly rolling horizon reviews with adaptive reallocation
Level 5 · Leading: Continuous rolling waves with real-time portfolio reprioritization

questions.q: How is the digital/technology value proposition perceived by the Board and CEO?
questions.hint: Strategic posture of IT in boardroom capital allocation decisions.

opts.text: Level 1 · Utility Cost Center: Subject to arbitrary across-the-board budget reduction targets
Level 2 · Operational Enabler: Funded primarily to keep the lights on and satisfy compliance mandates
Level 3 · Respected Service Partner: Dedicated funding allocated for business process automation
Level 4 · Strategic Growth Driver: Primary driver of customer experience, retention, and speed-to-market
Level 5 · Core Business Multiplier: Foundational board-level value multiplier and competitive differentiator

questions.q: Which Business Architecture & Strategic Mapping artifacts are active in practice?
questions.hint: Select all that are maintained, actively used, and reviewed with business stakeholders.

opts.text: Documented Enterprise Business Capability Model (Level 1–3 capabilities defined)
Value Stream Mapping tying customer journeys to underlying IT systems
Systems-to-Capability Heatmap highlighting technical health and redundancy
Domain Data Architecture models governed by designated business data stewards
Dynamic runtime telemetry linking business KPIs directly to system performance

questions.q: What is the primary structure of your technology delivery operating model?
questions.hint: Distinction between project-based handoff silos and dedicated cross-functional product squads.

opts.text: Level 1 · Siloed Waterfall: Rigid project-mode silos with painful cross-departmental handover chains
Level 2 · Component Teams: Component-based delivery teams with fragmented accountability and ticketing queues
Level 3 · Hybrid Matrix: Product squads piloted in digital channels, while core platforms remain in waterfall silos
Level 4 · Product & Platform TOM: Standardized product-and-platform operating model across core business domains
Level 5 · Scaled Product Flow: Scaled team topologies with autonomous squads, golden paths, and flow telemetry

questions.q: Rate maturity across your internal Developer Platform & Platform-as-a-Product capabilities:
questions.hint: Rate each sub-capability from 1 (Manual/Friction) to 5 (Autonomous/Golden Path):

subItems.name: CI/CD Golden Paths & Automated Deployment Pipelines
Policy-as-Code, Security Scanning & Automated Governance Guardrails
Platform Observability, Error Budgets & Developer Experience SLOs

questions.q: Rank your primary operational delivery bottlenecks (Drag or use arrows to sort from Biggest Bottleneck to Lowest):
questions.hint: Arrange the most significant organizational friction points impacting delivery speed:

rankItems.label: Manual Ticket-based Infrastructure Provisioning & Environment Delays
Ivory-Tower Architecture Approvals & Bureaucratic Stage Gates
Legacy Monolithic Deploy Freezes & Fear of Production Regression
Uncontrolled Shadow IT & Disjointed Engineering Standards Across Teams

questions.q: How seamlessly do business product owners and engineering squads collaborate?
questions.hint: Proximity of software engineering to end customer feedback and commercial decision-makers.

opts.text: Level 1 · Adversarial Handover: Business writes heavy specs and throws them over the wall to IT
Level 2 · Intermediated: Business analysts act as intermediaries with delayed feedback and mismatched intent
Level 3 · Nominal Participation: Product owners present in ceremonies but engineers remain insulated from customers
Level 4 · Co-Located Squads: True cross-functional product squads with shared customer empathy and weekly releases
Level 5 · Autonomous Commercial Squads: Empowered teams with direct authority to experiment, measure, and pivot

questions.q: How structured is your Application Portfolio Management (APM) & TIME scoring?
questions.hint: Tolerate, Invest, Migrate, Eliminate methodology applied across systems.

opts.text: Level 1 · Untracked: No central inventory; applications tracked across disparate informal spreadsheets
Level 2 · Static CMDB: CMDB contains system names but lacks business value, cost, or fitness ratings
Level 3 · Periodic Survey: Annual APM survey categorizing applications by high-level lifecycle tags
Level 4 · Active TIME Governance: Rigorous TIME framework actively driving retirement and modernization budgets
Level 5 · Real-Time Observability: Continuous real-time APM telemetry scoring cost, technical risk, and business fitness

questions.q: Rank the biggest areas of capability duplication & overlap across your business units:
questions.hint: Order from Highest Capability Redundancy to Lowest Redundancy:

rankItems.label: Multiple Disjointed ERPs & Core General Ledger Accounts
Fragmented CRM & Customer Master Data Repositories
Redundant Analytics Warehouses & Unsynchronized Data Lakes

questions.q: What percentage of your production applications run on supported/current vendor runtimes?
questions.hint: Operating systems, databases, runtime frameworks within N-1 supported vendor currency.

descs: Critical Exposure: Majority of production workloads running on end-of-life, unpatched runtimes
High Vulnerability: Severe legacy sprawl; multiple unsupported databases and core OS layers
Moderate Currency: Core systems maintained; peripheral applications lag in obsolescence
High Currency: Over 75% of production estate actively complies with N-1 support policies
Automated Currency: Continuous SBOM scanning, automated patch pipelines, zero EOL systems

questions.q: What is the architectural maturity of your enterprise integration backbone?
questions.hint: Decoupling between systems via APIs/events versus point-to-point batch files.

opts.text: Level 1 · Point-to-Point Spaghetti: Fragile direct database links, batch CSV exports, and scheduled FTP scripts
Level 2 · Monolithic ESB: Legacy on-prem Enterprise Service Bus creating an operational bottleneck
Level 3 · Hybrid APIs: Central API gateway with REST endpoints exposed for high-priority systems
Level 4 · Governed Event Architecture: Standardized API catalog combined with an enterprise event-driven backbone
Level 5 · Composable Mesh: Enterprise event mesh with published developer contracts, schema registries, and SLOs

questions.q: How quantitatively is technical debt measured and sized across the enterprise?
questions.hint: Financial and operational quantification of architectural compromises.

opts.text: Level 1 · Unmeasured: Tech debt is dismissed as engineer complaining; zero visibility into liability
Level 2 · Anecdotal Register: Informally maintained lists of legacy grievances with no financial sizing
Level 3 · Risk-Weighted Backlog: Documented tech-debt backlog with qualitative risk severity ratings
Level 4 · Quantified Balance Sheet: Fully sized debt register with estimated business remediation costs and outage risks
Level 5 · Boardroom Index: Tech Debt Index integrated directly into corporate risk registers and capital governance

questions.q: What percentage of annual engineering change budget is ring-fenced for debt paydown?
questions.hint: Dedicated capacity allocated for refactoring, architectural upgrades, and deprecation.

descs: Level 1 (0%): Zero capacity; 100% of bandwidth hijacked by emergency firefighting and feature demands
Level 2 (5-10%): Stealth refactoring performed by engineers informally during feature delivery
Level 3 (15-20%): Ring-fenced recurring capacity formally agreed between engineering and product leadership
Level 4 (25-30%): Continuous debt retirement built into every squad capacity model with measurable burndown
Level 5 (>35%): Transformational modernization sprint actively retiring monolithic liabilities

questions.q: Which Modernization & Decoupling Patterns are actively utilized in production?
questions.hint: Select all patterns currently executed with verified production workloads:

opts.text: Strangler Fig Pattern systematically hollowing out legacy monolithic systems
Domain Microservices with independent databases and deployment pipelines
Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform/CloudFormation) with automated immutable staging
Automated Regression Test Suites preventing deployment regressions without manual QA
Anti-Corruption Layers protecting new cloud architectures from legacy database schemas

questions.q: How is cloud modernization structured across your infrastructure estate?
questions.hint: Evolution from legacy on-premises data centers to cloud-native managed architectures.

opts.text: Level 1 · Data Center Lock-in: Legacy on-prem colocation with aging hardware and no cloud exit strategy
Level 2 · Unoptimized Lift-and-Shift: Virtual machines migrated to public cloud with inflated run costs
Level 3 · Hybrid Replatforming: Managed cloud services utilized for new initiatives; core estate on IaaS
Level 4 · Cloud-Native Containers: Containerized microservices, serverless components, and automated IaC
Level 5 · Sovereign & Multi-Cloud: Architecturally decoupled workloads optimizing cost, latency, and compliance

questions.q: How deliberate is your strategic sourcing model (In-House vs. SIs vs. SaaS)?
questions.hint: Clear segregation between strategic differentiating core and commoditized context capabilities.

opts.text: Level 1 · Accidental Sourcing: Reactive reliance on short-term contractor body-shopping without IP retention
Level 2 · Vendor Lock-in: Heavy dependence on a single systems integrator with no knowledge transfer
Level 3 · Documented Guidelines: Clear sourcing policy defining build vs. buy criteria for new projects
Level 4 · Core-vs-Context Segregation: Differentiating IP built in-house; context capabilities sourced via SaaS/partners
Level 5 · Dynamic Partner Ecosystem: Multi-vendor leverage with transparent benchmarking and continuous knowledge capture

questions.q: Rate operational resilience against Key-Person Dependency in critical systems:
questions.hint: Rate resilience from 1 (Extreme Single Point of Failure) to 5 (Fully Documented / Self-Healing):

subItems.name: Core Transaction Ledger / Mission-Critical Business Runtimes
Cloud Infrastructure, IAM Security & Network Routing
Integration Middleware, Legacy ETL & Data Pipelines
Proprietary Algorithms, Pricing Engines & Regulatory Reporting

questions.q: How effectively are critical software and cloud vendor renewals managed?
questions.hint: Commercial leverage, audit defense, and mitigation of punitive price escalation.

opts.text: Level 1 · Passive Renewals: Automatic renewals with zero leverage and frequent vendor audit true-up penalties
Level 2 · Last-Minute Sourcing: Procurement steps in 30 days prior with minimal time for architecture leverage
Level 3 · Centralized VMO: Vendor Management Office tracking renewal calendars and major license spend tiers
Level 4 · Strategic Vendor Governance: Proactive roadmaps, competitive benchmarks, and multi-cloud architectural leverage
Level 5 · Continuous Commercial Optimization: Real-time consumption telemetry, aggressive price gating, and exit options

questions.q: Which Technical Talent & Engineering Retention structures are established?
questions.hint: Select all active mechanisms in your engineering organization:

opts.text: Dedicated Fellow/Principal Technical Career Ladder (growth without managerial overhead)
Market-Benchmarked Compensation Parity for elite software and cloud architects
Internal Engineering Academy with protected hours for certifications and cross-skilling
Rotational Guilds & Communities of Practice sharing architectural standards
Active Open-Source contribution policy and engineering brand visibility

questions.q: Rank what actually drives project funding and capital approval in practice:
questions.hint: Order from Most Influential Driver of Project Funding to Least Influential:

rankItems.label: Executive Sponsor Clout & Political Loudest Voice in the Room
Urgent Regulatory Mandates & Imminent Compliance Deadlines
Exaggerated Upfront ROI Business Cases (Never Formally Audited)
Quantified Economic Value Added (EVA) & Customer Value Stream Telemetry

questions.q: How rigorously is business value tracked after modernizations go live?
questions.hint: Post-implementation review and verified realization of P&L benefits.

opts.text: Level 1 · Unaudited: Zero tracking post-launch; project success is declared purely if it goes live
Level 2 · Delivery Retrospective: One-time project close meeting focused strictly on schedule and cost variance
Level 3 · Qualitative Confirmation: Business sponsor submits an informal benefit memo after 6 months
Level 4 · Formal Finance Reconciliation: 12-month post-launch value realization audit reconciled against P&L results
Level 5 · Automated Telemetry: Continuous real-time value realization metrics directly linking software releases to revenue

questions.q: What is your Cloud Financial Management (FinOps) and unit economics maturity?
questions.hint: Visibility into technology unit cost per customer transaction, active user, or product line.

descs: Unallocated Overhead: Technology bills are a black box shared expense; zero accountability
Basic Bill Reviews: Monthly cloud invoice reviews with frequent bill-shock surprises
Enforced Tagging: Departmental cost allocation and showback implemented for major systems
Mature FinOps: Automated anomaly detection, rightsizing, and committed use discount coverage
Unit Economics: Real-time cost-per-transaction telemetry actively guiding engineering decisions

questions.q: How disciplined is your enterprise at terminating underperforming technology initiatives?
questions.hint: Stage-gate kill switches preventing zombie projects from consuming valuable capital.

opts.text: Level 1 · Sunk Cost Fallacy: Zombie projects funded indefinitely because 'we already invested too much'
Level 2 · Crisis Intervention: Projects cancelled only after multi-million dollar overruns trigger public embarrassment
Level 3 · Annual De-Scoping: Yearly portfolio reviews periodically pause or trim underperforming projects
Level 4 · Disciplined Stage Gates: Explicit off-ramps and criteria for project termination enforced at stage gates
Level 5 · Venture Capital Model: Fast milestones, fail-fast culture, and rapid redeployment of engineering capital
